sg.ra: Choose Center Orchestra rows E-J for some of the theater's best seats without being too close to the stage. These middle orchestra rows can cost less than premium orchestra seats.
Avoid rows A-C in Center Orchestra because they are too close to the stage. You may miss action at the sides, and the close view can be obstructed.
These are among the theatre's best seats, but premium mezzanine pricing is among the highest in the house.

sn.lo: Center Orchestra, rows A to C
sn.c: Rows A to C of the Center Orchestra are very close to the stage, and one seat guide says you can miss action at the sides.
sn.sh: Very close to the stage, so you can miss action at the sides

sn.lo: Orchestra, far sides, rows D to E
sn.c: At the outer ends of rows D and E, the boxes above slightly block the side of the stage.
sn.sh: The boxes above slightly block the side of the stage

sn.lo: Rear Mezzanine, rows D to G
sn.c: The back half of the rear mezzanine gets steep, which can bother anyone uneasy with heights.
sn.sh: Steep, which can bother anyone uneasy with heights

sn.lo: Center Front Mezzanine, rows D to E
sn.c: The back two rows of the Center Front Mezzanine are the good-value rows, and the rake keeps the view clear over the rows in front.
sn.sh: Lower price, and a clear view over the rows ahead

sn.lo: Center Rear Mezzanine, rows A to C
sn.c: The front rows of the rear mezzanine are among the cheapest seats in the house with a clean, raised view of the stage.
sn.sh: Among the cheapest seats, with a clean raised view

sn.c: Seats here are narrow with little legroom mid-row. Aisle seats in the Center Orchestra have the most room.
sn.sh: Narrow seats, and aisle seats have the most room

sn.c: The rear mezzanine is the most cramped level. Taller people should book an aisle seat.
sn.sh: The most cramped level, so tall people should take an aisle

vs.sum: The Ethel Barrymore Theatre offers good sightlines with a well-raked mezzanine and minimal obstructions, though some box seats have limited views. Sound quality is average, with some reports of less than ideal acoustics. Comfort is typical for a Broadway theater, with decent legroom in some areas. However, facilities are lacking, with only one restroom on the lower level leading to potential congestion.

acc.note: 5 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No steps from sidewalk. Infrared devices available.
